Topic.label: Integration and Practice: Quantitative Relationships in High-Speed Train Travel

Question: Two places are 600 km apart. The travel time t (h) and average speed v (km/h) of a high-speed train satisfy \(t=600/v\). If the travel time must not exceed 2.5 h, what is the minimum average speed in km/h?
Solution: \(600/v\le2.5\), with \(v>0\), so \(v\ge600\div2.5=240\). The minimum average speed is 240 km/h. When the distance is fixed, t is inversely proportional to v: the greater v is, the smaller t is.

Original.prompt: 两地相距 600 km，高铁行驶时间 t（h）与平均速度 v（km/h）满足 t=600/v。若要求行驶时间不超过 2.5 h，平均速度至少是多少 km/h？
Original.explanation: 600/v≤2.5，v>0，所以 v≥600÷2.5=240，平均速度至少 240 km/h。路程一定时 t 与 v 成反比，v 越大 t 越小。
